name: Eli Mason
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember painting carnival numbers on bare shoulders.” People around the downtown fountain know Eli by a small Sunday habit. Eli keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I drew it with house paint because the lifeguard had used up all our chalk.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a gray fisher's sweater and one cuff folded back twice. Eli has a straight nose and deep-set eyes, with short copper curls. Eli starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Eli uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Eli well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To preserve the paint recipe and its first date.
family: Eva Moss is Eli’s half-sibling. Eli makes room at the table. Eva brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *First shift back*, Eva says, “I visited the family off duty. I am learning which parts of that visit never belong in the break room.”
connections: Ivy Scott. They check whether the print came from the foot or the painter's brush.

reactions.situation: A child wants to trace a different sort of foot
reactions.response: Eli gives the child paper and room for a footprint that goes home with them.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Eli asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.
